item.title: Nine Days, Seven Deaths, No Lights: Inside Gary, Indiana's Slow Recovery From a 99-MPH Storm
item.body:
More than a week after a violent storm tore through northwest Indiana, tens of thousands of homes and businesses in Gary and across Lake County remain without electricity, and officials say full restoration is not expected until August 25.

According to local emergency management officials, the storm produced wind gusts estimated at 99 miles per hour, snapping or toppling hundreds of utility poles and pulling down power lines across the region. The scale of the damage has made this one of the longest widespread outages the area has experienced in years.

## A Widening Toll

Officials have linked seven deaths to the storm and its aftermath, though authorities have cautioned that some of those fatalities may be tied to conditions caused by the extended outage — such as extreme heat exposure and the use of alternative power or heating sources — rather than the storm itself. Investigations into the individual circumstances are reportedly still underway, and officials have urged residents and news outlets to rely on official statements rather than speculation as details are confirmed.

Local authorities have not released further identifying details about the victims, and residents are being asked to direct condolences and inquiries through official county channels.

## Schools Closed, Classrooms Dark

Gary-area school districts have remained closed since August 13, when the storm first knocked out power to campuses across the city. District officials have cited the lack of electricity, air conditioning, and reliable water pressure in some buildings as the primary reasons for keeping students home, with no firm date yet announced for reopening. Families have been advised to monitor official school district communications for updates on when classes will resume.

## Community Centers Become Lifelines

With many households still lacking power, refrigeration, and air conditioning during the late-summer heat, local community centers and municipal buildings have been converted into makeshift relief sites. Residents have been able to access:

- Hot meals distributed by community organizations and volunteers
- Charging stations for phones and small electronics
- Cooling areas to escape high indoor temperatures
- Basic supplies, including water and ice, distributed at select locations

City officials have encouraged residents who are medically vulnerable, elderly, or caring for young children to make use of these sites, particularly during peak daytime heat.

## Utility Crews Racing Against the Clock

Utility crews, reportedly supplemented by mutual-aid teams from neighboring states, have been working to replace downed poles, restring lines, and inspect damaged infrastructure across the affected footprint. Officials have said that the sheer number of poles requiring full replacement — rather than simple line repair — has significantly slowed the pace of restoration compared with typical storm recovery efforts.

Local utility representatives have said restoration is being prioritized based on the number of customers a given repair can restore, with hospitals, water treatment facilities, and other critical infrastructure receiving early attention, followed by neighborhoods with the largest concentrations of affected residents.

## What Residents Are Being Told

County officials continue to urge residents to:

- Avoid downed power lines and treat all lines as energized until confirmed otherwise by utility crews
- Report outages and downed lines through official utility and county hotlines rather than assuming crews are already aware
- Check on elderly or vulnerable neighbors, particularly during high-heat afternoons
- Discard refrigerated food that has been without power for an extended period, following official food-safety guidance

As the region approaches the projected August 25 restoration target, local officials have said they will continue to provide updates through official statements as repair work progresses. Residents are encouraged to follow verified local government and utility channels for the most current information on outage status, shelter locations, and school reopening plans.
